text.p: The Cyprus central bank on Monday approved a half a percentage point reduction in commercial deposit and lending rates, it said in a statement.
The cut, effective Tuesday, lowers deposit rates to 6.5 percent from 7.0 percent and rates for new loans to 8.0 percent from 8.5 percent.
The rates for existing loans will change on July 18, the central bank said. The central bank decision takes the form of a directive which commercial banks follow.
A central bank official told Reuters the decision to cut the interest rates was taken during a meeting of the bank's board of directors earlier Monday.
Coperative credit societies, which operate independently from the central bank, are expected to abide by the new rates, the central bank official said.

"They did express some reservations but we do expect them to follow the commercial banks," the central bank official told Reuters. "Their position was that if the central bank approves it (the reduction) they will follow."
Co-ops currently have one third of the local banking market, both in terms of deposits and outstanding loans.
The association of commercial banks has publicly supported the move to reduce rates.
One banker said a reduction in rates would help reinvigorate business activity and absorb excess liquidity in the banking system.
Under a 1944 law there is a nine percent ceiling on interest rates, first imposed by the former British colonial rulers to curb usury.
The government is edging towards deregulating interest rates and relaxing capital flows before accession talks begin to join the European Union, scheduled to start next year.
Commercial interest rates were last reduced in two stages in 1994, with a 50 basis point cut in the deposit rate followed some months later by a 50 basis point cut in lending rates.
